title: Meaning and extrinsic evidence: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Pacific Gas & Electric Co. v. G.W. Thomas Drayage & Rigging Co.: It provides the contextual side of the course’s comparison with New York’s more restrictive treatment of extrinsic evidence.

W.W.W. Associates, Inc. v. Giancontieri: It explains why strong evidence about negotiations may fail to affect a result under a rule that gives a clear writing controlling force.

Greenfield v. Philles Records, Inc.: It shows concretely why identifying the governing law precedes applying a general statement about contractual interpretation.

Trident Center v. Connecticut General Life Insurance Co.: It connects the interpretation debate to the hierarchy of authority: a federal court’s preferred rule does not replace controlling state substantive law.
